doctrine: Align rooftop PV installation with roof life: never put panels on a roof with under 10-15 years of remaining service life without a re-roof plan, or the removal/reinstall cost destroys the economics
Boring-proven rooftop PV beats novel storage chemistries or exotic mounting systems; battery storage should be justified by demand-charge or resiliency economics, not added by default
Under NNN leases, tenant consent and cost allocation must be resolved before origination proceeds — PV feeding tenant meters or common-area load changes the lease pass-through math
Measured baseline: use actual peak-demand and TOU billing data to size PV/storage against real demand charges, not a modeled irradiance-only estimate
Maintainability: local O&M contractor availability for the specific inverter/battery brand matters as much as the equipment spec sheet
Sequence after load-reduction measures where feasible — a smaller, cheaper PV/storage system sized to a reduced load is preferable to over-building generation against an unoptimized building

EV charging always carries owner MAKE-READY capex (electrical service/panel, conduit, trenching) even under a third-party host agreement (Blink/ChargePoint fund hardware, not make-ready) — never model a $0-capex EV line. Size added revenue against an explicit utilization assumption; the electrical service-capacity ceiling is the binding constraint. EV is an NOI/revenue play (capitalized ancillary revenue, risk-adjusted), not a carbon measure.
origination_prompts: Is the roof rated for at least 10-15 more years of service life per the PCA, or is a re-roof already planned/budgeted?
Does the property have high demand charges or TOU rate exposure per the utility bill structure? Storage-economics candidate.
Is the property NNN with tenant metering — does the lease structure allow landlord-owned PV to offset tenant load, or does it need tenant consent/amendment?
Is there available roof area and structural capacity (per PCA structural notes) unencumbered by rooftop mechanical equipment?
feasibility_checks: Confirm roof structural load capacity for PV racking, especially on older commercial roofs with unknown live-load margins
Verify interconnection queue timelines and utility net-metering/export rules for the market before committing to a payback model
Under NNN leases, confirm tenant consent process and how PV output will be metered/allocated before quoting savings to ownership
Check local permitting and inspection timelines via Shovels for solar contractors — some markets have multi-month backlogs that change the staging plan
Tenant disruption for PV install is typically none/light (roof-level work); storage equipment rooms may require light common-area access coordination
Roof warranty: PV penetrations can void NDL roof warranties — require roofer-of-record coordination or ballasted/non-penetrating racking
data_requirements: roof age, remaining useful life, and structural capacity
12-month interval/TOU utility data with demand charges
lease structure and tenant metering configuration
